html:
The beginning of Rome, which Roman tradition dated to 21 April 753 BCE, when Romulus marked out the city on the Palatine Hill. The date was worked out centuries later by the scholar Varro.

In the legend, the twins Romulus and Remus were thrown into the Tiber, suckled by a she-wolf and raised by a shepherd. They quarrelled over where to build, and Romulus killed his brother. He filled his city with outlaws and, in the tale of the Sabine women, seized wives for them. Later writers such as Livy (History of Rome) also tied Rome to the Trojan hero Aeneas.

Archaeology tells a slower story. Huts stood on the Palatine and nearby hills from around the 10th century BCE, and the villages grew together into a town, influenced by the Etruscan cities to the north and Greek traders to the south. Seven kings followed Romulus by tradition, among them Numa Pompilius, until the last king was driven out in 509 BCE.
sum: The beginning of Rome, which Roman tradition dated to 21 April 753 BCE, when Romulus marked out the city on the Palatine Hill. The date was worked out centuries later by the scholar Varro.
